leftEvidence.title: The assembly weeps and proposes a return to Egypt

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: The whole assembly cries through the night, complains against Moses and Aaron, and asks why the LORD brought them to die.
points.right: Moses says the people would not go up, rebelled, and accused the LORD of hating them and bringing them out for destruction.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: They say wives and children will become prey and propose appointing a leader to return to Egypt.
points.right: He recalls answering that the LORD would fight as in Egypt and carry them as a man carries his son, yet they did not believe.

payload.posture: Both witnesses preserve fear, refusal, and desire to reverse the journey.

rightEvidence.title: The retelling centers refusal, accusation, and fear

payload.tension: Numbers foregrounds the assembly’s night of weeping and children-as-prey claim; Deuteronomy foregrounds accusation that the LORD hated them and Moses’ remembered answer.
payload.title: The refusal in Numbers and Deuteronomy
